record.paper_title: 20 Open Questions About Deformations of Compactifiable Manifolds
record.original_question: How should one compare the notion of cobordism with the notion of deformation for compact complex manifolds?

evidence.quote: Question 2. Compare the notions of cobordism and deformations of compact manifolds.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Two compact complex manifolds $X_0$ and $X_1$ of the same complex dimension are said to be deformation equivalent if there exist a connected complex manifold $\mathcal{X}$ and a proper holomorphic submersion $\pi:\mathcal{X}\to B$ over a connected complex base $B$ such that $X_0$ and $X_1$ both occur as fibers $\pi^{-1}(b_0)$ and $\pi^{-1}(b_1)$. Two compact (stably) complex manifolds are said to be (complex) cobordant if their disjoint union bounds a compact (stably) complex manifold with boundary.

Develop a precise comparison between the equivalence relation of deformation and the equivalence relation of (complex) cobordism on the class of compact complex manifolds. In particular:

(a) Determine whether deformation equivalence implies complex cobordism, and conversely whether complex cobordism (with appropriate stably complex structure) implies deformation equivalence, providing proofs or explicit counterexamples in each direction.

(b) Identify intermediate equivalence relations or refined invariants (for example, those built from Chern numbers, Hodge numbers, or holomorphic Euler characteristics) that are simultaneously cobordism invariants and deformation invariants, and characterize the discrepancy between the two relations in terms of such invariants.

(c) Formulate and prove a structural statement describing how the deformation equivalence classes of compact complex manifolds sit inside the complex cobordism classes.
artifact.status_search_result: The problem is a broad open-ended comparison question. While classical results (Chern numbers as cobordism invariants, deformation invariance of Hodge numbers in special cases) provide partial answers, no comprehensive comparison between deformation equivalence and complex cobordism for compact complex manifolds appears in the literature. The question remains open as a research program.

status_evidence.title: Complex bordism - Manifold Atlas
status_evidence.snippet: Two stably complex manifolds are bordant if and only if they have identical sets of Chern characteristic numbers.
status_evidence.claim: Cobordism is detected by Chern numbers, providing one side of comparison, but deformation invariance is more subtle.

status_evidence.title: Cobordism - Wikipedia
status_evidence.snippet: Complex cobordism is the bordism theory of stably complex manifolds.
status_evidence.claim: Standard framework for complex cobordism uses stably complex (not complex) structures, indicating the comparison with holomorphic deformations is nontrivial.
